findings: R3-F01 RESOLVED as a tooling artifact, close it: the browser tool's accessibility tree (read_page) never prints an <input> value. On /profile it renders `textbox "Email"` and `textbox "Your name"` bare, while the DOM holds the real email (17 chars) and "tools" respectively and the screenshot shows both. Four reads — first load, reload, new tab, away+Back — all non-empty. No app defect; future runs must read input values with javascript_tool, never from read_page.

Signed-in visitors to the three retired auth addresses land on Home, not on a visible /login: the 308 → /login first hop is real (proven unauthenticated by curl), and /login then bounces a signed-in session to /. Anyone re-testing SIGNIN-A4 from inside a session will see Home and must not read that as a miss.

Content-hash collision across tenants is normal on staging and must not be mistaken for a leak: contentHash f31d4a36…0c76 has seven Asset rows under seven different orgs, founder included (row 01M265PG7GFKWNMK1F8B3KVDD4, 2026-09-10). Fetching /files/u/founder/<that hash>.jpg served A's own copy. The honest probe is a B-only hash under A's namespace — fe1873ef…1c75 under u/founder/ — and R2 answered NoSuchKey. Blobs are namespaced per owner; guessing a hash yields nothing you do not already hold.

apps/web/app/files/[...key]/route.ts gates the inline GET on keyOwnerMatches() plus the allowlist, and only the ?download=1 branch also checks a live Asset row (ownerId + deletedAt: null). So an inline link inside your own namespace presigns without a DB row check. Not cross-tenant exploitable (namespace gate holds, proven above), but it means an old inline link to a soft-deleted asset may still resolve. UNVERIFIED as behaviour: staging has zero soft-deleted founder assets, so it could not be tested — code read only.
